title: No permutive sub-stitch in a harmony's stitch, and the coset census
claim: Proved by hand (the advisor model's two-constant-fibres lemma, rechecked): a harmony's one-order stitch holds no permutive sub-stitch on a set of two or more states, so no orbit's stitch pairs hold a ratio subgroup (the additive automaton of Ledrappier-type influence), a Z2 x Z2 block or a free pair, at any period, for any two-way knot shape and slot order; the odd harmonies 61, 73, 193 included. Exact: 73 harmonies (span <= 8, every period; the 7 odd step sets), 187 orbits: no free site, no ratio subgroup, 22 + 2 degenerate subgroups and cosets, no coset with a ratio part, so lagged stitches hold none. After the run: the same on 32 harmonies of span 9. Referee pending.
failure_conditions: A permutive sub-stitch on one set of states in a harmony's stitch.
A harmony in range with a free site.
A coset with a ratio part that a fresh census finds.
remaining_obligations: Independent referee (the background referee thread): pending.
foundation_claim_scope: The plain not-all-equal law; every harmony for the theorem; for the census, the 66 harmonies of span <= 8 at every period and the 7 odd step sets of ODD-FAMILY (and 32 of span 9 after the run), stitched in one order, unlagged or lagged.
